newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish navy vessels to visit north Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy vessels to visit north Cyprus.

text.p: Six Turkish navy vessels will visit the breakaway Turkish Cypriot state this week for celebrations of the 23nd anniversary of the Turkish invasion of the island, Turkish Cypriot security forces said on Thursday.
The ships will dock on Friday at the Kyrenia harbour on the Turkish part of the Mediterranean island for the two days of celebration ceremonies, a security forces statement said.
The chief of the Turkish air force, General Ahmet Corekci, is also to attend the ceremonies, it said
Turkey sent its troops to the northern part of the island on July 20, 1974, in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup backed by the military then ruling Greece.
Cyprus has since been partitioned into Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot sections. The leaders of the two communities held talks in the United States last week.
Turkish Deputy Prime Minister Bulent Ecevit, who ordered the 1974 invasion and is still regarded as a hawk on the Cyprus issue, is also expected to visit the island at the weekend.
Turkey maintains around 30,000 troops in the north.
